newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania okays new Merrill terms for oil credit.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania okays new Merrill terms for oil credit.

text.p: Lithuania has decided to accept new conditions set down by Merrill Lynch for a $19 million loan to buy oil for its Mazheikiai refinery, a government spokesman said on Wednesday.

The government refused to guarantee the loan after Merrill altered the terms of the credit. Instead of 0.75 basis points over Libor plus a formula tied to the price of oil, Merrill asked simply for Libor plus two basis points.
But the spokesman said the government changed its mind and decided to accept the new conditions. He did not give a reason for the government's change of heart.

The credit is to be split into two $9.5 million portions and will be used to buy oil supplies for the refinery, which suffers from many down-days due to problems with supplies from Russia, from where all its oil comes.
The Merrill credit is meant to pave the way for a $40 million loan from Chase Manhattan, which the refinery hopes to get without a government credit.
